description: Mitigations for structural and ground collapse. Trench shoring is the dominant control for excavation — the #1 collapse killer.

mitigations.name: trench_box
mitigations.description: Prefabricated trench shield or hydraulic shoring system. Prevents trench wall collapse onto workers. Required by OSHA for trenches >5ft (1.5m). The primary engineered control.
mitigations.pfd_source: PFD 0.05. Failure: not used (most common — time/cost pressure), undersized for trench depth, not extending above trench edge, moved without re-shoring.
mitigations.effectiveness_source: When correctly sized and installed, prevents soil from reaching workers. Very high effectiveness. OSHA: most trench fatalities occur in unshored trenches.

mitigations.name: sloping_benching
mitigations.description: Excavation walls cut to a safe angle (depends on soil type — OSHA soil classification A/B/C). Eliminates vertical walls that can collapse. Design mitigation — inherent to the excavation shape.
mitigations.pfd_source: PFD 0.03. Failure: incorrect soil classification (Type C assumed as Type A), slope angle too steep, water ingress weakening slope, surcharge loads too close to edge.
mitigations.effectiveness_source: At correct angle for soil type, wall collapse is prevented by geometry. The most reliable excavation protection when space permits.

mitigations.name: scaffold_design_check
mitigations.description: Scaffold designed by competent person, erected to design, inspected before use and after adverse weather. NASC/TG20 for tube and fitting. Prevents overload/structural failure.
mitigations.pfd_source: PFD 0.10. Failure: design inadequate for load, erected differently from design, not inspected, altered after inspection (boards removed, ties missing).
mitigations.effectiveness_source: Competent design and inspection prevents structural scaffold failure. Effectiveness is indirect — ensures scaffold is fit for purpose.

mitigations.name: temporary_works_coordinator
mitigations.description: BS 5975 temporary works management — coordinator ensures design, check, installation, and removal of temporary works (formwork, falsework, propping, shoring).
mitigations.pfd_source: PFD 0.12. Administrative role. Failure: role not assigned, coordinator not competent, design not checked, early striking of formwork.
mitigations.effectiveness_source: BS 5975 process ensures temporary structures are designed and checked. Most formwork/falsework collapses result from process failures that a TWC would catch.

mitigations.name: competent_person_excavation
mitigations.description: OSHA-required competent person to inspect excavation daily, after rain, and after any change. Identifies deteriorating conditions before collapse.
mitigations.pfd_source: PFD 0.12. Failure: person not competent (titled but not trained), inspection skipped, conditions change between inspections.
mitigations.effectiveness_source: Daily inspection catches deteriorating conditions (water ingress, cracking, surcharge loads). Effectiveness depends on inspector competence and response to findings.

mitigations.name: rescue_from_collapse
mitigations.description: Trained rescue team with shoring equipment for trench rescue. Post-collapse — victim is buried, team must shore and dig without causing secondary collapse. Time-critical: traumatic asphyxia kills in minutes.
mitigations.pfd_source: PFD 0.25. Specialised capability rarely available on site. Failure: no rescue plan, fire service (primary responder) not trained in trench rescue, secondary collapse during rescue.
mitigations.effectiveness_source: Even with trained team, survival from full burial in soil is low — soil weight prevents breathing within seconds. Effectiveness is strongly time-dependent. Partial burial has much better rescue outcomes.
